_readme: Consumption audit trail for UT-N (2026-09-08). Every template with a local consumer repo under C:\dev must list EVERY Type="Variable" Target it declares, each with a one-line citation of where the consuming repo actually reads and USES it (not just declares it). tests/test_variable_consumption.py enforces that the two lists (template vs. this file) match exactly, and that a template flagged no_local_consumer carries no per-var entries. This file does NOT re-derive consumption on its own (this repo's CI has no checkout of the private consumer repos) — it is the durable record of the audit a human/worker performed, so a Variable added without one is caught structurally instead of silently accreting. Every citation starts `reads <VARIABLE>`: the exact env-var name the code looks up, not just the feature it serves. For a pydantic-settings field that name is env_prefix + the field name (case-insensitive unless case_sensitive=True; an alias / validation_alias replaces it), so field backup_db_user with no prefix reads BACKUP_DB_USER, never DB_BACKUP_USER. A pydantic citation names a `field <name>`, and the test checks that every `field <name>` in a citation, and every lookup written as ${NAME}, os.environ.get('NAME'), os.environ['NAME'], getenv('NAME') or process.env.NAME, spells the Variable; other shapes, such as a project's own _env('NAME') wrapper, are not checked, and neither are env_prefix, aliases or case_sensitive=True, since no consumer uses them. If the name the code looks up is not the Variable, the Variable is read by nothing: fix the template, not the citation. Re-measure and update the citation whenever the corresponding line in the consumer repo moves.
